title: Center a dual-handle apple wedger over an apple and press it level through to the cutting board
instruction: Drive the apple wedger level through the apple flush onto the cutting board so all eight wedges separate, keep the apple where it stands, and clear both grippers.
context: Every daily snack prep or family meal uses a handheld apple slicer to portion fruit on a cutting board. The slicer has two side grips 50 mm either side of its coring tube; pressing only one grip against the cut resistance of eight seams rolls the blade ring past 5 deg and binds it in the flesh, whereas balanced two-sided downward pressure drives all eight blades through to the board together.
setup: A fixed solid maple cutting board (203 x 305 x 19 mm, 8 x 12 x 0.75 in) sits centered at (0.360, 0.000) m on the station tabletop. A 66 mm Granny Smith apple (54 mm tall, 150 g) stands on the board at its center. On a fixed dark silicone staging mat (130 x 210 x 3 mm) at (0.185, 0.000) m sits an OXO Good Grips 32681 apple slicer, corer and divider: a dual-grip stainless 8-blade wedger, 114 mm blade span, 80 g, with an 8-sided 23 mm OD hollow coring tube, eight radial 1.2 mm blades and two cushioned side grips at +-49 mm. One fixed starting layout; arms start at ready pose.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial; the run succeeds once 1.0 holds for 3 s. Measured at trial end with a ruler and a digital protractor: count the separated wedges, measure the ring bottom above the board and the wedger tilt. 1.0: all 8 wedges separated (every seam cut through), each wedge at most 12 mm from where it stood, the wedger ring resting on the board within 1.5 mm and level within 5 deg and within 10 mm of the apple center, and both grippers more than 120 mm clear of wedger and apple for 3 s (60 steps). 0.75: as 1.0 with the clear hold shorter than 3 s. 0.50: ring on the board and level, at least 6 of 8 wedges separated, or all 8 separated with a gripper still within 120 mm. 0 otherwise (doing nothing, sweeping, dropping off-center, knocking a wedge off its seat, a one-hand cocked jam, or a press that stops short of the board). Possible scores: 0.0, 0.50, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Lift the wedger off the board, discard the cut apple, stand a fresh conditioned apple (see README specimen spec) on the board center, wipe the blades and board dry, and place the wedger level on the dark staging mat at x = 0.185 m, y = 0.000 m with its grips along Y.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (PhysX, 20 Hz control); eight rigid wedges plus a core plug, each glued. The blades and coring tube pass through the fruit without collision and cutting force is not modelled (accepted #699 convention). The cut is a geometry-gated rule on the wedger pose: a seam releases only when its blade is within 2.5 mm and 6 deg of the seam plane and driven through to the board, level within 5 deg. A tilted ring releases nothing (DEVIATIONS).
